title: Cycle Oxygen Protocol and Scope Deflation Guidelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define an operational protocol ("Cycle Oxygen") that preserves minimal delivery capacity during mid-cycle shocks and prescribes a deterministic scope-deflation path so teams can safely decommit work while protecting critical SLAs and OKR outcomes.
background: Recent cycles showed repeated mid-cycle staffing shocks (on-call burn, hiring delays, cross-org urgencies) that caused ad-hoc scope cuts, unclear stakeholder tradeoffs, and downstream regressions in reliability metrics. PMs and Eng leads have requested a lightweight, playbook-driven framework to make decommit decisions reproducible and fast.
goals: Create a single-page decision protocol that engineering and PM leads can run in <30 minutes during a shock
Standardize a three-tier scope deflation ladder (Protect, Preserve, Pare) with concrete heuristics
Automate capacity signals into the Console: a "breathability" score combining FTE availability, critical-cycle-queue length, and SLO risk
Reduce emergency mid-cycle scope churn by 60% in the next two cycles
scope: Deliver runbook, triage checklist, routing for approvals, and a lightweight on-call rotation adjustment template. This does NOT include automation changes to the capacity estimator (that will be a follow-up project).
deliverables: Scope deflation ladder with examples applied to current initiatives
Decision checklist and template emails for stakeholder comms
Console dashboard prototype showing breathability score and recommended action
stakeholders: Engineering leads: Lucas Moreno, Jae Kim
GTM lead: Rafael Ortiz (for customer messaging)
success_metrics: % of mid-cycle decommits executed via the protocol (target >= 80%)
Reduction in unplanned rollback incidents (target -50% next cycle)
Mean time to decision during a shock <= 30 minutes
Stakeholder satisfaction score >= 4/5 in post-cycle retrospective
timeline: Week 1: Draft runbook and scope ladder; interview 6 Eng/PM leads
Week 2: Prototype Console breathability visualization and run internal dry-run
Week 3: Iterate based on dry-run feedback; finalize comms templates
Week 4: Run two cross-team simulations and publish Confluence + training session
decisions: Use three-tier ladder (Protect / Preserve / Pare) instead of percentage-based trimming to simplify enforcement
Escalation path: Eng lead + PM sign-off required for Preserve; Director-level sign-off required for Pare
Breathability score will be a heuristic (availability, queue length, SLO delta) with manual override
Automated enforcement (cancelling CI runs, gating releases) is out-of-scope for MVP
updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff completed; interviewed 6 Eng leads; common pain: lack of clear stakeholder ordering
2026-02-25: Draft scope ladder posted to Drive (drive.redwood.com/s/CycleOxygenDraft); asked teams for example use-cases
2026-03-03: Console prototype wireframe uploaded (noted latency constraints when querying multiple team queues)
2026-03-08: Dry-run with Runtime and two product squads; identified need for a fast 'safety-net' fallback when dependencies cross teams
2026-03-12: Incorporated feedback; updated escalation matrix and added a 'dependency veto' clause for infra-critical items
risks: Teams may treat the ladder as a checklist and over-prioritize speed over quality
Breathability heuristic could amplify false positives if upstream queues are misreported
Cross-team dependencies may require faster exec-level escalation than the runbook provides
Customer communication may lag if GTM is not looped early
